title: pattern-kata: Memento save/restore round-trip (reuse the Delta-migration engine)
description:
License: E4 UNIQUE-capability axis — "migration is the one capability
with no conventional counterpart: loud lost-data counterexamples,
unsupported-inverse proofs" (DESIGN SS6; kata-10). This is the strongest
license in the suite. ploeh analogue: none needed — this is catherine's own
round_trip non-invertibility proof applied to a new domain.
Hypothesis: a legacy Memento implementation (OSS undo/redo, snapshot
persistence, session restore) modeled as a schema map has save/restore
== a Delta reindexing pair; the existing round_trip analysis proves
non-invertibility BY NAMING the field/state that fails to return —
i.e. silent data loss on restore becomes a loud, witness-backed finding
BEFORE it is hit in production.
Fault matrix: dropped field on restore; lossy serialization of an optional;
version-skew restore (old snapshot, new code).
Negative control: full-fidelity snapshot (identity map) — tool must report
zero lost data and no false finding.
Kill condition: if conventional diff-based testing catches the same losses
at comparable cost, the "no conventional counterpart" claim is falsified ->
killed in ledger (this would amend E4; cite the ledger entry).
Status: HYPOTHESIZED — pre-register first.
notes: REVIEW 2026-11-13 (issue-review pass): blocked-by catherine-1od — P11 builds the probe ledger kind + Delta conventional-baseline arm this kata's kill condition ('conventional diff catches same losses') requires; the 'no conventional counterpart' framing is UNMEASURED until P11's baseline exists (E4 claim stays as-is but inherits 1od's epistemic caveat). Lane: DESIGN (target pick + model derivation + pre-registration) then AFK (fault-matrix runs + ledger). complexity:l.

title: gates: hook exit-code fix is not durable — bd init regenerates swallowing wrappers
description: Fixed today by hand: .beads/hooks/{pre-commit,pre-push,prepare-commit-msg} now propagate lefthook exit codes (call_lefthook || exit). But these files are bd-generated (BEGIN/END BEADS INTEGRATION markers); the next bd init re-appends the beads block after call_lefthook WITHOUT exit capture, silently disarming pretender/ah/spk gates again. Options: (a) upstream fix in beads hook template, (b) ddl doctor check that flags the swallow pattern (grep call_lefthook line followed by unchecked continuation), (c) lefthook.yml-side workaround. Also realigned versions.ddl.toml pins (pretender 0.10.0, wai 2026.10.19, openspec 1.15.0, ah 0.12.0 added) — keep ddl doctor verifying them.
notes: Chosen approach (from failure-taxonomy review): option (c) self-defending gate — add a lefthook pre-commit command OUTSIDE the ddl-managed block that greps .beads/hooks/{pre-commit,pre-push,prepare-commit-msg} for the '_lh_exit' capture pattern after call_lefthook and fails with a remediation hint if the swallow pattern returns. Keeps the fix durable across bd init regenerations without waiting on upstream. Still worth filing the upstream beads issue as option (a).

title: P8: rule lens — rules as subobjects with resolution policy (HYPOTHESIZED)
description: Phase 8 of docs/DESIGN.md §4.4. Rule presentation over the input domain X: rules as decidable predicates (subobjects R_i), policy = order-enrichment (PriorityOrder/FirstMatch/DeclaredDisjoint), effective region E_i = R_i \ u_{j<i} R_j. Findings: gap (uR_i != X), overlap (intersection without policy), shadow (E_i empty), derivable (R_k = R_i AND R_j). Equivalence-checkable simplification via distinguish (same total action on X, witness inputs otherwise). Rule discovery: examples + predicate vocabulary, partition-equivalence check. Attribute columns + decidable expression language (int/bool/string comparisons, AND/OR/NOT, mod) enter the kernel here. Epistemic status HYPOTHESIZED: precedent above the floor (Rust exhaustiveness, DMN hit policies) but no ct-catlab-class evidence. RED: no rule presentation type; findings not expressible. GREEN: gap/overlap/shadow/derivable findings on an enumerable domain are exact via P4 bounded search; distinguish proves or refutes rule-table equivalence with witnesses. REFACTOR: predicate expression language scoped to decidability; presentation JSON in model document. Validation (pre-registered): one kata ABOVE the triviality floor (10-20 compound rules + priority policy, pricing/eligibility table) + one second negative control NEAR the floor; killed if no unique detections above the floor. GATED on P6 (catherine-9vv) recording the schema-lens negative control first.

title: pattern-kata: exploratory weak-lens set (Observer, Bridge, Flyweight, Command, Prototype)
description:
License: E5 (LLM proposes, tools evaluate) only — E4 grants NO purchase
for these; each is an explicitly cheap hypothesis-or-kill probe with a
hard effort cap (1 session each), filed together to avoid ticket noise.
- Observer as notification monoid: fan-out order determinism/dedup

- Bridge as axis independence: the two variance dimensions modeled as

- Flyweight as quotient/identity: shared instances equal-but-not-identical;
  fault = identity/equality confusion detected via dangling/shared-row
  analysis. Negative control: no sharing.
- Command as invertibility: undo stacks as composition with inverses;
  fault = non-invertible command silently corrupting undo (round-trip
  probe reuses kata-15's machinery). Negative control: fully invertible set.
- Prototype as clone independence: shallow-clone aliasing = shared mutable

outcome (killed in ledger) — E4 predicts most die; the ledger records it.

title: pattern-kata: negative-control bundle — the no-lens patterns must stay honest
description:
License: E4's honest boundary is the license ("buys nothing for..."
validated negatives; the FizzBuzz self-negation gate is a release gate).
Purpose: the patterns with NO plausible universal-abstraction lens must be
modeled anyway, and the tool+procedure must yield the "model this
conventionally" verdict — a lens that fires here is a FALSE POSITIVE and
falsifies the disposition.
Set: Facade (interface narrowing, no algebra), Singleton (unique-object
globality; at best a terminal-object anecdote), Mediator (centralized
pairwise interactions; no executable law), Template Method (fixed skeleton
with holes; no kernel-checkable law), Abstract Factory / Factory Method
(creation has no composition algebra; family-mixing is a typing question
the instance layer already handles).
Expected ledger verdict for EACH: no categorical advantage (the FizzBuzz
precedent, generalized from one control to a bundle).
Fault matrix: none seeded — the fault to catch is OURS (a lens firing
where it should not).
Kill condition: if any of these yields a structural-unique detection,
the A/B/C disposition is amended and the finding promoted to a real
hypothesis ticket. Status: HYPOTHESIZED (and the suite's honesty gate).

title: Versioning: adopt wild contracts (accretion/break verdicts) — retire the SemVer promise
description:
CHANGELOG.md declares 'adheres to Semantic Versioning' and Cargo.toml carries 0.1.0, but the SemVer promise is vacuous here: nothing is on crates.io and the only planned distribution (P9 bogart pilot) builds from source at a pinned rev. Decision (2026-11-11, with sasha): manage versions with wild contracts instead of semver labels — 'version numbers are claims, wild replaces them with checks' (wild is already this repo's canonical-JSON/hash donor, so the precedent exists).

Scope v1 — wild is a prototype: only its "extract" and "check" subcommands are implemented (init/adopt/publish are designed-not-built), so adopt at shadow level only:

1. RED first: golden test pinning the extracted contract of a tagged revision (`wild extract .` -> contract JSON; store contracts/ per release; test asserts extract output matches the stored normative example byte-for-byte, same discipline as the hash.rs port).
2. GREEN: contracts/ + a check step comparing each revision against its predecessor (accretion / break / unknown verdicts recorded per revision); wire `wild check` into ci.yml as shadow — verdicts reported, never failing the build.
3. Retire the SemVer claim: CHANGELOG header drops 'adheres to Semantic Versioning'; release tags become lineage/revision-hash tags, not vX.Y.Z; Cargo.toml keeps its cargo-required version field as a vestige (wild native level never modifies package/tag/version).

Escalation to gate level (reject breaks in CI) waits until wild ships init/adopt gate — file a follow-up then, do not hand-roll it.
